subject: Post-call: Dedicated GPU fit, isolation needs & SLA alignment
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Park <apark@vectorai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated GPU fit, isolation needs & SLA alignment

Hi Alicia / Marcus —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap while it's fresh, and a proposed set of next steps so we can keep momentum toward a dedicated/reserved pool that meets VectorAI's latency and compliance needs.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Production latency SLO: P95 <= 180ms for text-generation workloads (batching expected).
- Unit cost target: reduce per-token CPU/GPU cost vs current self-hosted baseline by ~30% via pooling + KV caching.
- Isolation: evidence of strict tenancy isolation and audit logs (SOC2 scope) required for PHI-adjacent pipelines.
- Scale: peak inference concurrency expected ~1,200 qps (short spikes to 2.5k) — need burst/queueing plan.

What Redwood recommended on the call
- Dedicated reserved GPU pool (multi-GPU islands) with tenant isolation and optional private VPC control plane.
- Autoscaling buckets + burst capacity to handle spike patterns; queueing policy to preserve P95 SLO under load.
- KV cache + prefix caching to shave steady-state token costs.
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime target for production endpoints; expedited incident routing and runbook access.

Immediate open questions we noted
- Exact throughput profile by model and sequence length distribution (you mentioned GPT-style generation + embedding pipelines). Can you share sample qps/seq-length split?
- Procurement preference: monthly commitment vs 12mo committed?
- SOC2 + audit evidence timing: when do you need certification artifacts for procurement?

Proposed next steps (owners)
- VectorAI: send a 7-day sample traffic dump or an exported traffic histogram — Alicia / Marcus
- Redwood (Ben): draft a tailored pricing estimate and burst-capacity proposal — Ben
- Redwood (Naomi): prepare an ops readiness doc (runbook + required monitoring hooks + SOC2 artifact list) — Naomi
- I'll consolidate answers and a short mutual action plan for signature by next Tue (2025-03-18).

Attachments: initial SLA draft + ops checklist attached (PDF + runbook stub).

Thanks — talk soon,

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0179

--

From: Alicia Park <apark@vectorai.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lee <mlee@vectorai.com>, procurement@vectorai.com
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated GPU fit, isolation needs & SLA alignment

Thanks Dylan — helpful summary, appreciate the structure. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Traffic sample: we'll pull a week of requests and share a simple CSV with qps by minute + average sequence length by endpoint. Expect that to land by EOD Mon (2025-03-17).
2) Procurement: VectorAI prefers a 12-month committed model for price predictability, but we may want an initial 3-month pilot window. Can you outline both options in the estimate?
3) SOC2: procurement wants the SOC2 report and evidence of encryption-at-rest keys in your offering. Timeline: we need artifact links by handshake (target 2025-03-24) to start internal review.

One operational note: we run an embedding pipeline that hits your system at higher qps but lower per-request token counts — that matters for batching strategy.

Cc'ing procurement to keep the thread in view. We'll expect Ben's pricing and Naomi's ops write-up.

—Alicia
Alicia Park
Head of ML Ops, VectorAI
apark@vectorai.com

> On Mar 14, 2025, at 3:12 PM, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> > Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap while it's fresh...
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Park <apark@vectorai.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Mar 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated GPU fit, isolation needs & SLA alignment

Alicia — Dylan, Naomi — thanks. I'll take the lead on pricing and will include two commercial paths: a 12mo committed plan with a pilot option, and a shorter term reserved pool with slightly different burst pricing.

What I'll include in the estimate:
- Baseline monthly committed seats (GPU count) and per-token unit economics with/without KV caching.
- Burst credit model for short spikes (pricing and throttling rules).
- Ops uplift cost for SOC2 evidence packaging and private VPC (if chosen).
- Proposed SLA boundary: 99.9% uptime and a 15-minute P1 response window for the dedicated pool (we can soften if legal procurement requires).

I'll draft the proposal and share by Tue EOD (2025-03-18). If you can push the traffic histogram by Mon EOD as mentioned, that will let me size the pool more accurately.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

--

Quick check-in — following up on the action items: 

- Alicia / VectorAI: any ETA on the traffic export? If it looks like Monday slip, that's OK but please let us know so we can adjust timing.
- Ben: thanks — please include a short table of latency impact at different queue sizes in the estimate.
- Naomi: attaching the ops-runbook-stub with the monitoring hooks we suggest (trace IDs, token-level cost drift alerts, and a fallback routing policy).

I've attached an updated SLA draft with a note calling out the SOC2 artifact timeline and an appendix describing burst behavior (how queuing is handled versus immediate rejection). If procurement at VectorAI prefers a redline, happy to set a quick 30-min call for that.

Next internal step: Ben to own commercial proposal; Naomi to own ops package; I will coordinate a 30-min pricing + ops sync with VectorAI after you review the docs. Proposed meeting window: Thu 2025-03-20 10:00–10:30 PT.

Thanks all —

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
